title: Dynamic Range Ladder
description: A clickable vertical amplitude ladder placing clipping, headroom, working range, noise floor, and silence on one continuous scale, with an add-a-bit toggle demonstrating the 6 dB per bit rule.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Audio Engineering
Quantization

educational.topic: Dynamic range, headroom, and the noise floor
learningObjectives: Interpret the relative positions of full scale, headroom, signal, and noise floor
Explain what happens to a signal in each zone
Explain what an additional bit of depth changes and what it does not
prerequisites: A sample is stored as a fixed-width integer

controls.label: Any band
controls.purpose: Show its definition and the consequence for a signal there

controls.label: Add 1 bit of depth
controls.purpose: Lower the noise floor about 6 dB and grow the usable range

assumptions: Band heights are illustrative rather than logarithmically to scale
The noise floor is treated as set by quantization alone
limitations: Real noise floors are dominated by analog and thermal noise well before the quantization limit is reached, so added bits stop helping at some point

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Single persistent spatial layout explored by click
keyQuestions: Which boundary moves when you add a bit — full scale or the noise floor?
Why does headroom cost you signal-to-noise ratio?
commonMisconceptions: That more bits let you record louder signals
That clipping, headroom, and noise floor are unrelated concepts
assessmentOpportunities: Compare a 16-bit and 24-bit recording that clip identically
